name: Shell Bags
location: Windows XP: NTUSER.DAT: Software\Microsoft\Windows\ShellNoRoam\BagMRU and \Bags. Windows Vista and later: NTUSER.DAT: Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU and \Bags, plus UsrClass.dat: Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\BagMRU and \Bags
purpose: Stores Windows Explorer's per-folder view preferences (icon size, view mode, window position). As a side effect of tracking which folder each preference belongs to, it preserves a record of every folder a user has browsed in Explorer, including folders on removable media, network shares, and mounted volumes that no longer exist on the system.
key_fields: BagMRU - a tree of numbered subkeys mirroring the folder hierarchy the user navigated (each numbered key = a path segment), with binary shell item ID list data encoding the folder name and, for many item types, timestamps
MRUListEx (in each BagMRU node) - binary value giving the access order of child folders at that level
NodeSlot - value inside a BagMRU node linking it to its corresponding view-settings entry under Bags
Bags\{slot}\Shell - view mode, icon size, sort column, and window position/size for the referenced folder
normal_baseline: A tree reflecting the user's ordinary folder navigation habits: profile folders, Documents/Downloads/Desktop, commonly used application data folders, and drive letters the user routinely opens.
anomalies: Shellbag entries referencing removable drives, mounted encrypted volumes, or network shares that are no longer present on the system and have no corresponding entry in current MountPoints2/USBSTOR-if the volume genuinely never existed on this host, this points to remnants worth cross-referencing
Folder paths referencing staging directories, archive tool output, or exfiltration-style naming shortly before a data-loss event, even though the folder itself has since been deleted
Shellbag entries for folders on a device that was connected only briefly or outside expected business hours

A gap in shellbag timestamps/structure inconsistent with the account's normal usage pattern, suggesting selective deletion of BagMRU/Bags entries (uncommon since most cleanup tools do not target these keys)
Folder access evidence in shellbags with no corresponding Prefetch, RecentDocs, or Jump List activity, indicating the folder was browsed but its contents were not opened through the expected channels
anti_forensic_notes: Shellbags are not commonly targeted by mainstream privacy-cleaner tools, so they frequently retain folder-access history well after the corresponding files, folders, or removable/network volumes are gone-making them one of the more resilient sources of historical folder-browsing evidence. They exist in two hive locations (NTUSER.DAT and UsrClass.dat on Vista+), so an incomplete acquisition that only captures one hive will miss part of the picture.
